Step 1

Pick Your Plan

Three ways to vote. Pick one, say it out loud, and it is a plan.

  • Vote Early

    Oct 6 to Nov 1

    At your county board of elections. No appointment. Bring your photo ID.

    My plan is to vote early at my county board of elections this week.
    Find my county board

  • Vote Absentee

    Request by Tuesday Oct 27, 8:30 pm

    Your ballot must be back at your county board of elections by Tuesday Nov 3, 7:30 pm. No photo ID needed.

    My plan is to request my absentee ballot today and send it back the day it arrives.
    Request an absentee ballot

  • Vote on Election Day

    Tuesday Nov 3, 6:30 am to 7:30 pm

    At your polling place. If you are in line at closing, you vote. Bring your photo ID.

    My plan is to vote at my polling place on Tuesday Nov 3 before 7:30 pm.
    Find my polling place

Step 3

Bring Your ID

Ohio asks for a photo ID to vote in person. Check your wallet now.

Accepted

  • Ohio driver's license or state ID (unexpired; an old address is fine if your current address is in the pollbook)
  • BMV interim ID form
  • U.S. passport or passport card
  • U.S. military ID
  • Ohio National Guard ID
  • U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs ID

Not Accepted

  • Out-of-state license
  • Student ID
  • Utility bill or bank statement
  • Digital ID on a phone

Good to Know

  • A free Ohio state ID is available at any BMV agency.
  • The name on your ID must match the name on your registration.
  • No photo ID is needed to vote absentee. The request form takes a license number or the last four of your Social Security number.
